title: Errors and failure

outcomes.can: Tell a thrown error from a successfully returned empty value.

intro: A missing task can be an ordinary result your callers expect. A failed reader may instead throw an exception. A throw interrupts ordinary execution until a catch handles it. try surrounds the operation that might throw. In strict TypeScript the caught value is unknown: JavaScript permits throwing strings as well as Error objects.

steps.title: Trace the example
steps.text: If the reader returns an empty string, the try block returns that value normally. Only a throw enters catch. instanceof Error narrows to the class with a message field. A typeof check can separately recognize a thrown string. Other values need a fallback. Returning inside try or catch finishes the current call.

steps.title: Explain a caught value
steps.text: Return the Error message for an Error, the original text for a string, and "Unknown" otherwise. Preserve empty messages.

choices.feedback: Returning empty text is a successful return.

questions.prompt: If the reader throws the string "No file", which text does this example return?

choices.feedback: A string is not an Error instance.
